title: Project state machine
description: One file per QA objective. The single source of resumable truth for a project.

environment.description: Environment class. production, shared and unknown hold phase 9 until a human grants an `environment` decision, because mutating tests against the wrong system cannot be undone.

authorised.description: Claim that testing this target is authorised. Layers 7 and 8 additionally require a granted `authorisation` decision in spec/decisions.json; this flag alone is not enough, because an agent can set it.

source_document.description: Project-relative path of the requirement copied into requirements/.

layers.description: Enabled test layers. Disabled layers are excluded from coverage denominators.

framework.description: The project ACTUAL toolchain, discovered rather than assumed. The harness core is stack-agnostic. For a brownfield target the existing stack is the default: never introduce a new framework or language without a recorded justification in selection. Popularity and familiarity are not justifications.

_placeholder.description: Present only in the untouched template. Phase 0 must run stack discovery against the real target and either confirm this stack or replace it, then REMOVE this flag and record selection. A project still carrying _placeholder has not had its stack decided, it has inherited one.

language_version.description: The runtime or compiler version the suite must actually run under, not merely typecheck against.

e2e.description: e.g. playwright, selenium, webdriverio, cypress, puppeteer, robot-framework, none

mobile.description: e.g. appium, espresso, xcuitest, maestro, detox, none

api.description: e.g. playwright-request, supertest, requests, restassured, karate, newman, none

perf.description: e.g. k6, jmeter, gatling, locust, artillery, lighthouse, none

runner.description: e.g. playwright-test, pytest, vitest, jest, xunit, testng, junit, rspec, go-test

build_system.description: e.g. npm, pnpm, yarn, maven, gradle, pip, poetry, dotnet, bundler, cargo

selection.description: Why this stack. Required once _placeholder is removed. This is the record that stops a future session quietly re-deciding the toolchain, and stops this one defaulting to whatever it knows best.

decision.description: For a brownfield repository USE_EXISTING_FRAMEWORK is the default. NEW_FRAMEWORK_REQUIRED against an existing stack demands strong evidence, not convenience.

reason.description: Evidence-based. "Repository uses Maven, TestNG and Selenium 4 with 180 existing tests" is a reason. "Playwright is modern" is not.

discovered_from.description: What you actually inspected: package.json, pom.xml, build.gradle, requirements.txt, existing test directories, CI config. An empty list means the stack was assumed.

greenfield.description: True only when the target genuinely has no existing automation. Verify before asserting it.

existing_assets.description: Reusable fixtures, page objects, helpers and clients found in the target. Reuse beats create.

decided_at.description: ISO-8601. Date, or date-time. Length alone is not a date.

counters.description: Idempotency counters. Rerunning a phase must not increment these twice for the same artefact.

created.description: ISO-8601. Date, or date-time. Length alone is not a date.

updated.description: ISO-8601. Date, or date-time. Length alone is not a date.

mode.description: new: project created under ~/testharness-projects/<slug>. existing: QA artefacts in <repo>/qa/ beside the user's own test repo.

suite.description: Where the test project lives. Mode new: relative to the project directory, normally 'suite'. Mode existing: relative to the repo root (the parent of qa/), recorded by phase 5 discovery. Agents may write test code only here.

runner_cwd.description: Directory the runner is invoked from, relative to suite.path. Defaults to '.'.

latest_run.description: Newest run id under runs/. Set only by bin/qa-runs.mjs.

status.description: No 'warn'. G1 to G4 are blocking under CLAUDE.md section 8: a blocking gate either passes or stops the pipeline. A warn here would let a run continue past a gate that did not pass, which is the one thing the gate exists to prevent.

evaluated_at.description: ISO-8601. Date, or date-time. Length alone is not a date.

run.description: Run id whose gate file produced this verdict.

warningGate.description: G5 session_score only. CLAUDE.md section 8 makes this the single warn-only gate: below threshold it warns and the pipeline continues, because an honest low score is information rather than a reason to stop.

evaluated_at.description: ISO-8601. Date, or date-time. Length alone is not a date.

run.description: Run id whose gate file produced this verdict.
